newsitem.title: GUINEA: Guinea civil service audit holds up salaries.
newsitem.headline: Guinea civil service audit holds up salaries.

text.p: Civil servants in Guinea used to receiving their salaries promptly have yet to get their pay for August because of an ongoing audit to root out phantom workers.
The government launched a nationwide operation on August 28 to rid the its payroll of fictitious workers as part of new prime minister Sidia Toure's campaign to cut spending.

Government officials said on Monday salaries would be paid at the end of the operation on September 15. They said inspectors had unearthed a large number of fictitious names on the payroll in all ministerial departments, but gave no figures.

The names include people who work in the public service without being officially employed. More commonly they are workers long dead or who never existed. Their salaries end up in the pockets of a clique in the service.
The government has put the annual wage bill at 171 billion Guinean francs ($171 million) -- 50 percent of current state expenditure.
Toure, who took office in July, plans to cut public service spending by 30 percent by the end of the year as part of measures to revive the economy.
